Here, the variable limit $x$ appears as the lower limit of integration. To apply FTC II directly, we prefer the variable on the upper limit. Using the property of definite integrals, we rewrite

$$
{\int }_{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{2})\,\text{d}t=-{\int }_{2}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{2})\,\text{d}t.
$$

Now, by FTC II we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{2})\,\text{d}t & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{\int }_{2}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{2})\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{2}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
